hypothēca, hypothēcae f.

noun, first declension

a mortgage

A pledge of land or a house, as against pignus, a pledge of movable things (Lewis & Short). To take out a mortgage, hypothēcam obligāre; to pay it off, hypothēcam līberāre (Traupman 347).

Examples

  • hypothēcam līberāre

    to pay off a mortgageTraupman 347

  • hypothēcam obligāre

    to take out a mortgageTraupman 347

  • hypothēcā obligāre

    to mortgageTraupman 347

See also bank account, rent, pay in instalments.
